<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="אייר_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518918549_theRebbe_741" batchId="meluket-_D7_90_D7_99_D7_99_D7_A8_meluket__BH_POST_1766518918549_theRebbe_741__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section contains the opening header and date for Lag BaOmer 5745.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Lag BaOmer 5745*</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that just as praises of the Creator arouse His will to bestow, so too praises of Rashbi were necessary to arouse his incomparable influence.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">To understand the concept of Rashbi,</t>
    <t s="1">it is known the discourse of Lag BaOmer of the Rebbe Maharash1</t>
    <t s="2">(the one who taught "lechat’chilah ariber"2),</t>
    <t s="3">that what we find in the Zohar3</t>
    <t s="4">that they praised Rashbi with awesome praises4,</t>
    <t s="5">such as Rabbi Yehudah would call him "Shabbat"5,</t>
    <t s="6">and "Who is Panai"6</t>
    <t s="7">"The Lord God, that is Rashbi"7,</t>
    <t s="8">this is understood from the concept of the praises with which they praise the Creator, may He be blessed,</t>
    <t s="9">for at first glance it is perplexing,</t>
    <t s="10">does He, may He be blessed, need our praises8?</t>
    <t s="11">And the explanation of this is known9,</t>
    <t s="12">that because all the worlds are incomparable to Him, may He be blessed,</t>
    <t s="13">and the flow of influence to the worlds is a descent relative to Him, may He be blessed,</t>
    <t s="14">therefore, in order to arouse in Him, may He be blessed, the will to bestow upon the worlds, it is through praises.</t>
    <t s="15">And this is what our sages, of blessed memory, said10</t>
    <t s="16">"A person should always arrange the praise of the Omnipresent and then pray,"</t>
    <t s="17">for although prayer is a positive commandment from the Torah to request one's needs from the Holy One, blessed be He11,</t>
    <t s="18">and the commandment of the Torah is a granting of power,</t>
    <t s="19">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="20">there must first be an arrangement of the praise of the Omnipresent,</t>
    <t s="21">through which they arouse in Him, may He be blessed, the will to bestow the needs of the one who praises.</t>
    <t s="22">And similarly, this is also regarding Rashbi,</t>
    <t s="23">that due to the extreme greatness of Rashbi relative to the other Tannaim,</t>
    <t s="24">that he was separate from them in an incomparable manner,</t>
    <t s="25">therefore,</t>
    <t s="26">in order to arouse his influence,</t>
    <t s="27">they needed to praise him.</t>
    <t s="28">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="29">that what is said in the discourse, that the concept of the praises of Rashbi is understood from the concept of the praises of the Omnipresent,</t>
    <t s="30">is in addition to bringing proof that in order to arouse an influence that is incomparable, praises are needed,</t>
    <t s="31">but rather also,</t>
    <t s="32">that the incomparability of the other Tannaim relative to Rashbi is analogous to the incomparability of the created being relative to the Creator.</t>
    <t s="33">And this is also what is said in the discourse, that they praised him with awesome praises,</t>
    <t s="34">for the word "awesome" indicates a matter that is completely separate in value,</t>
    <t s="35">to the point that it inspires awe.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that Rashbi served as the intermediary between the level of "Eitan" and the Tannaim, who are the foundations of the Oral Torah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">B)</t>
    <t s="1">And the concept is,</t>
    <t s="2">that it is written12</t>
    <t s="3">"And the Eitanim, the foundations of the earth,"</t>
    <t s="4">Eitanim is the letters of Tannaim13,</t>
    <t s="5">and they are the founders14</t>
    <t s="6">of the Oral Torah, which is called by the name "earth"15,</t>
    <t s="7">meaning that they draw down the aspect of Eitan into the Oral Torah.</t>
    <t s="8">And it can be said that the drawing down of Eitan to the Tannaim is through Rashbi,</t>
    <t s="9">for he was the intermediary between the aspect of Eitan and the Tannaim,</t>
    <t s="10">as is explained at length in the discourse16.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
